versionSource: Best-effort reconstruction from earliest-attested Hijazi-script manuscripts: Tübingen Fragment Ma VI 165 (radiocarbon-dated 649-675 CE) for Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ; Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328 + St. Petersburg / Birmingham / Vatican fragments, late 7th c. CE Hijazi script) for Sūrat al-Qamar and Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah. Modern Cairo recension (1924 King Fuad edition) supplied as reference text for the rasm-to-vocalized comparison.
sourceCitation: Sadeghi, Behnam, and Bergmann, Uwe, 'The Codex of a Companion of the Prophet and the Qurʾān of the Prophet' (Arabica 57, 2010, pp. 343-436) — the foundational radiocarbon and codicological study of the Sanʿāʾ 1 palimpsest. Sadeghi, Behnam, and Goudarzi, Mohsen, 'Sanʿāʾ 1 and the Origins of the Qurʾān' (Der Islam 87, 2010, pp. 1-129) — the transcription of the Sanʿāʾ 1 lower text. Hilali, Asma, The Sanaa Palimpsest: The Transmission of the Qur'an in the First Centuries AH (Oxford 2017). Déroche, François, Qur'ans of the Umayyads (Brill 2014) and La transmission écrite du Coran dans les débuts de l'islam: le codex Parisino-petropolitanus (Brill 2009). Neuwirth, Angelika, Scripture, Poetry, and the Making of a Community: Reading the Qur'an as a Literary Text (Oxford 2014). Reynolds, Gabriel Said (ed.), The Qur'ān in Its Historical Context (Routledge 2008/2011, 2 vols). Corpus Coranicum project (Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities) for the digital comparative apparatus.

subtitles.en: Suras 21:1–5, 54:1, 56:15–24 — the three citations the Raëlian canon engages, sourced from the oldest known Hijazi-script Qur'anic manuscripts (mid-7th c. CE)

descriptions.en: Qur'an 21:1–5, 54:1 and 56:15–24, the three passages the Raëlian canon cites, translated from the oldest Hijazi-script manuscripts of the 7th century, with notes.
descriptions.verificationNote: This translation is produced from a best-effort reconstruction of the rasm based on published facsimiles of Tübingen Ma VI 165 and Codex Parisino-petropolitanus, and the Corpus Coranicum digital apparatus. The rasm is well-attested for the target ayahs and stable across the early Hijazi-script witnesses. Verification of the precise letter-skeleton against the original codicology (Tübingen UB; BnF Paris; National Library of Russia St. Petersburg; Cadbury Research Library Birmingham; BAV Vatican) is pending. Variants where the early manuscripts differ from the modern Cairo recension are noted per ayah; the Hafs reading-tradition is supplied as the reference vocalized text.
descriptions.scriptNote: Three layers per ayah are preserved in the source file: (1) the **rasm** (bare consonantal skeleton from the earliest manuscript, no dots, no vowel marks — what the scribe actually wrote, before letter-discrimination dots and vowel-marks were added); (2) the **modern vocalized Arabic** (Hafs ʿan ʿĀṣim reading-tradition, Cairo recension 1924) supplied as the reference vocalization; (3) **scientific transliteration** (DMG / ALA-LC convention). The early manuscripts also lack ayah-numbering marks; the divisions follow the standard Cairo enumeration.
descriptions.lensRiskNote: Qur'an translation carries a distinctive lens-risk landscape: (a) the Raëlian canon's explicit citations of these three passages — Sura 54:1 *inshiqāq al-qamar* 'splitting of the moon' read as ET-propulsion-event in *Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet*; Sura 56:15-24 read against the orientalist-houris-stereotype with the WoH paradisal-reception layered on top; (b) the Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-Allah reading (popular-fringe; explicitly disavowed); (c) Christian-supersessionist pre-resolution (no 'hour-draws-near = Day of the Lord' Christian-typology pre-resolution); (d) orientalist-stereotyping of Sura 56's *ḥūr al-ʿīn* (the 'wide-eyed' paradise-companions); (e) the manuscript-criticism dispute (Wansbrough vs Crone-Cook vs Sadeghi-Goudarzi vs Hilali) preserved-not-adjudicated. The WoH-Translation engages Islam respectfully and technically; the Editor and Reviewer pipeline produces named-scholarship attributions at every claim site.
